public_rationale: The September 13, 2026 review describes scoped training restrictions and partial resumptions, while leaving contract cancellations and cash effects unknown [e1]. It does not establish an actual contraction in OpenAI and Anthropic's combined compute demand, the condition needed to test this forecast [e1]. Nor does it document the predicted material downward changes in both revenue and backlog at every affected counterparty [e1].
limitations: The cited review predates the September 14 claim and does not establish subsequent demand or financial changes through October 28.
The packet does not verify the labs' claimed share of AI compute demand or the $748 billion backlog baseline.
No complete set of attributable revenue and backlog adjustments is documented.
The forecast supplies no deadline, adjustment lag or numerical materiality threshold. Missing evidence of contraction does not establish that none occurred.

statement.excerpt: As OpenAI and Anthropic make up the vast majority of AI compute demand, any contraction of that demand would mean material restatements of revenue (and the $748 billion in revenue backlogs) across every hyperscaler, along with the neoclouds and any other counterparty.
statement.document_title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands

from_speaker: OpenAI and Anthropic make up the vast majority of AI compute demand
the neoclouds and any other counterparty
our_interpretation: The antecedent is an actual contraction in OpenAI and Anthropic's combined compute demand. A training pause, slower growth or lower token prices alone does not establish it.
Every refers to each affected compute counterparty, including hyperscalers and neoclouds. It describes the scope of the predicted consequence, not a separate antecedent.
In ordinary financial commentary, restatements may mean downward revisions. Formal corrections of previously issued financial statements are a narrower alternative reading.
The $748 billion is a stated backlog baseline, not a predicted loss of that entire amount.
The required metric_scope describes the quantified backlog stock. Revenue is a separate flow and would require separate matched evidence.
No accounting basis, backlog measurement date or response deadline is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: After a verified demand contraction, every affected counterparty reports material downward changes in both revenue and backlog attributable to that contraction, using comparable measures.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a verified contraction and a completed contractual and reporting adjustment cycle, at least one affected counterparty demonstrably has no material downward change in one of the claimed measures.

evidence.explanation: This secondary review expressly limits what the earlier pause disclosures establish. It neither proves a later demand contraction nor shows that no contraction occurred.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Consistent measurements establishing a contraction in combined demand, followed by comparable disclosures for every affected counterparty. Support requires material reductions in both revenue and backlog attributable to that contraction across all affected counterparties. Contradiction requires at least one affected counterparty with no material downward change in at least one claimed measure after its contractual and reporting adjustment cycle is complete. The demand-share premise and $748 billion baseline also require verification.
